title: good company
hookLine: an old man cramming grammar, a teacher's song, and the first step toward freedom

cards: In the holy city of Varanasi, the story goes, the teacher Shankara was walking with his students when he heard an old man reciting rules of Sanskrit grammar, over and over, driving them into his memory.
The man was near the end of his life, and he was spending it on grammar. Shankara was moved, and a song came out of him. Worship Govinda, worship God, foolish mind.
When your time comes, the rules of grammar won't save you. That song is called Bhaja Govindam. And one of its verses answers the question anyone would ask next.
If not more rules, where do you start? It answers like a row of dominoes, each step knocking over the next, all the way up to freedom. The first domino isn't more study.

teach.b: Satsang. Sat means true, real, good. Sang means company, being together.

teach.h: GOOD COMPANY, THEN LETTING GO, THEN FREEDOM.
teach.b: Satsang is good company, the company of what's true and of people turned toward it. Here's the song's chain, in plain words. From good company comes letting go.
From letting go comes freedom from delusion. From freedom from delusion comes a mind that stays steady. And from a steady mind comes freedom while you're still alive.
Delusion: think of the snake on the rope. Freedom: yesterday's moksha.
And the thing that starts it all isn't a technique, or another rule to memorize. It's a room. In Hindu life, a satsang is often an actual gathering.

People meet in a home or a temple hall to sing, to hear a teacher, to read a text together, to sit in silence side by side. Nobody has to be advanced. It's part of why so many Hindus don't only pray alone; they gather.

teach.h: WE TAKE THE SHAPE OF OUR COMPANY.
teach.b: Underneath the verse is a simple idea: company shapes a person. A friend's worries can become your worries; a grandmother's patience can become your patience.
So the question is yours: what is your company doing to you, and how much time do you spend near what's true? That first domino has a name and a face.

how: Hindus gather for satsang in homes, temples and ashrams to sing bhajans, hear a teacher, read scripture together and sit in silence, and some families hold one on special days.

games.q: Nani's dragging me to the thursday satsang at the Mehtas' house. 2 hours of bhajans 😐 why can't i just pray in my room like a normal person
o: you can pray alone too. but the old verse says good company is the first step: the people you sit with shape you.
praying alone doesn't count in Hinduism.
satsang is just a party with snacks.
games.why: Shankara sang that grammar rules won't save the old man in Varanasi, and that good company is the first step toward freedom. That's satsang: Priya's room is fine, and the room full of singers shapes her too.

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.

s: in the Bhaja Govindam chain, the first step is years of hard study
the first step is good company. letting go, clarity and freedom follow.
a satsang can be an actual gathering in a home or temple
people meet to sing, hear a teacher, read together and sit in silence.
you have to be advanced to join a satsang
nobody has to be advanced. you come, you sit, you listen.

games.q: you're the old man in Varanasi, and Shankara's song says the grammar rules won't save you. by the song's row of dominoes, where do you start?
o: a long retreat alone in the mountains.
games.why: Bhaja Govindam starts with satsang: from good company comes letting go, and the chain runs all the way to freedom while living.

practice: Here's the practice: sit in company. Bring to mind one person whose presence makes you steadier. A friend, a grandparent, a teacher, someone in a story.
Let their face come. Notice what happens to your breathing near them. Then widen it to everyone, anywhere, singing or sitting in a satsang today.
If you like, hum the song's first words under your breath, bhaja Govindam. If you pray, you can hold them all before God. The bell holds the time.

wordCard.voice: Satsang. Good company. The company of what's true, and the first domino on the way to freedom. Twentieth word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: sat, true or good, and sanga, company. The company of what's true.

carryVoice: Your line: good company changes you. Today, spend ten unhurried minutes with one person who steadies you. In person, if you can. Day twenty.

sources.ref: Bhaja Govindam, verse 1 (grammar rules will not save you when the time comes), with the traditional story of its composition at Varanasi
Bhaja Govindam (Moha Mudgara), verse 9, traditionally attributed to Adi Shankara
